title: Rulers: without ends, bond distance grows linearly
claim: Rulers without ends. (1) If a law on Z^d splits at range D (finite sets more than D apart have independent projections), every knot is D-chained, so bond distance >= sup separation / D and a bond ball of radius r has at most |T|(2Dr+1)^d variables. (2) A parity law whose finite moves are dense (a law without ends) splits at the diameter of a generating set of its finite moves. (3) Tseitin's law on Z^D has d_inf <= bond distance <= (2D-2)(d+1)+1, and the gauge law on Z^2 has 2d+1 <= bond distance <= 2d+7 (d = graph distance), so bond balls grow like r^D: the lattice's dimension is read from allowed states alone, and on the plane the ruler is taxicab. On the atom thread w(t-1) & L(t) -> w(t), the bond distance between witnesses w_s, w_t is exactly t-s+1, and every knot through them contains the loops between. (4) A parity law with one distinction per site is free or has no finite moves. (5) With Ledrappier's law on x, z free and y = x+z, every variable is flipped by a finite move, yet y and z at 0, 2^k e1 and 2^k e2 form a knot for every k: per-variable nativity does not give a ruler. (6) Conservative extensions never increase bond distance.
failure_conditions: A knot of a splitting law that is not D-chained, or a bond ball leaving the sup-norm ball of radius Dr.
A parity law with dense finite moves and two finite sets more than D apart whose joint projection is not the product of their projections.
A gauge or Tseitin bond distance outside the stated bounds, or a thread bond distance different from the number of loops between the witnesses.
A nonzero finitely supported allowed state of a nontrivial one-type parity law.
The six-variable set of the product law failing K1-K3, or a variable of it that no finite move flips.
A knot of a law that stops being a knot under a conservative extension.
foundation_claim_scope: Laws on Z^d with finitely many distinctions per site (and finite boxes of them); bond distance as defined in NATIVE-NETWORK-20261021-001. Uniform statements by proof; finite checks on 8x8, 6x6, 7x7, 41x41, 4^3 and 7^3 boxes, thread windows of 5 loops, 39 random one-type laws, and Ledrappier patches up to side 8.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: prose proofs; check.py runs nine checks, each with a rejected control; the knot search was cross-checked against an independent min-cost-flow shortest cycle; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found: items 1-2 are a finite-set form of strong irreducibility and of dense homoclinic groups giving specification (Lind-Schmidt 1999; Lind-Schmidt-Verbitskiy 2013), and item 4 is the integral-domain argument behind Ledrappier's example; the delta is the consequence for minimal implied constraints (bond distance as a ruler whose growth gives the lattice's dimension), the exact thread distance, and item 5 on the source-aware reading.
